title: PriS privacy-requirement record
description: Machine-readable representation of the principal PriS concepts: a privacy requirement, the privacy goal it expresses, the organisational goal it affects, the process that realises that goal, the Privacy Process Pattern applied to the process, and the candidate Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs). Formalises the template in Listing 1 of the manuscript (adapted from Diamantopoulou et al., 2017). Property names, including spaces and capitalisation, follow the published template so that existing PriS JSON files validate unchanged.

privacy requirement.description: One record per privacy requirement under analysis.

optionalReference.description: Title of a related goal or process. An empty string means that no such element exists (e.g. a leaf goal has no child goal).

privacyProperty.description: PriS privacy requirements and the corresponding Privacy Process Patterns: the eight reference requirements of Kalloniatis et al. (2008) plus undetectability (Diamantopoulou et al., 2017). Extensions (e.g. GDPR-oriented patterns) should be added in a new schema version rather than by relaxing this list.

optionList.description: Numbered alternatives, as in the published templates: "Option 1", "Option 2", ... Numbering should start at 1 and be consecutive (checked by tools/validate.py, not expressible in JSON Schema).

Title.description: Organisational goal affected by the privacy requirement, optionally with its identifier, e.g. "... (G3.3)".

Decomposition type.description: AND/OR decomposition recorded for the goal, as in the PriS goal model. Empty string if not applicable.

Title.description: Process (or subprocess) that realises the affected organisational goal, e.g. "Collect Responses (P4.3)".

Process Pattern.description: Name of the Privacy Process Pattern applied to the process. Must match the "Name" of a pattern record (see pris-privacy-process-pattern.schema.json).

Privacy Enhancing Technologies.description: Subset of the pattern's implementation techniques considered suitable for this organisational goal and context. May be empty while the fourth PriS activity (identification of implementation techniques) is still open.
